description: Funds $1,522,600 for Dutch Elm Disease response.
Funds $250,000 for urban forestry vehicles.

chips.text: Approved
11 for, 0 against
Dutch Elm Disease cases escalated rapidly from 4 in 2023 to 41 in 2025.
The city must transition from preventive efforts to an active long-term management model.
Long-term financial plan for Dutch Elm Disease management remains unclear.
SOS Trees supported the budget request and outlined strategy.
Unmanaged communities may lose 18% of Elms annually; strong management slows losses to 2%.
Administration will provide seasonal updates on Dutch Elm Disease management.

description: City acquires 130 Idylwyld Drive North for a drop-in center.
Costs $1.635 million, federally funded; $350,000 for renovations.
325 Avenue C South location remains open until new site opens.

chips.text: Approved (7-4)
7 for, 4 against
Councillor Dubois questioned why a 250-meter buffer for daycares wasn't applied like for schools.
Businesses and residents near 130 Idylwyld Drive North expressed safety and operational concerns.
City Solicitor clarified shelter buffer is Council resolution, not a bylaw.
Using the Affordable Housing Reserve for renovations is an exception to Council policy C03-003.
Councillor Dubois requested a detailed budget for the $350,000 renovations.
Speakers cited increased security costs, vandalism
Councillor Davies cited daycare proximity and lack of a better solution as reasons for opposition.
A speaker raised concerns about potential liability due to the daycare's proximity.

speakers.name: Kristine Wilkinson
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Decision to Purchase 130 Idylwyld Drive North Building
said: Proposed center two doors down from her optometry clinic.
Temporary shelter caused $15,000 security costs, tenant left.
Asks for compensation plan if council proceeds with location.

speakers.name: Ryan Wilkinson
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Proposed Purchase of 130 Idylwyld Drive for Drop in Shelter
said: Invested in corridor based on city's Imagine Idylwyld Drive Plan.
High-quality tenants won't lease next to 24-hour crisis hub.
Asks city to protect vision it invited investors to support.

speakers.name: Shawna Nelson
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Acquisition of 130 Idylwyld Drive North for Drop-In Location
said: Avenue C is better, with 20+ essential services nearby.
130 Idylwyld was available earlier; no comparative analysis provided.
Concerns about daycare across street, lack of transparency, due diligence.

speakers.name: Terry Novakovski
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Proposed Shelter 130 Idylwyld Drive North
said: Opposed to purchase; city keeps making mistakes with locations.
Shelters cause decline, vandalism, crime, decreasing property values.
Concerns about daycare across street and potential liability.
